newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher as packers compete for hogs ahead of another expected heat wave, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
"They're trying to get as many hogs under the belt while they can," one central Iowa hog buyer said.
Farmers also were moving hogs ahead of the heat, he said.
Midwest temperatures were seen in the upper 90s degrees Fahrenheit or hotter through this week, several dealers said.
"This may be the coolest day of the week," a southern Minnesota hog dealer said of Tuesday's temperature readings.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $58.50 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 for hogs delivered to the plant, but could firm as temperatures rise during the day, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 higher at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $60.50 at plants, with a possibility of $61.00 later, they said.

Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $58.50 in the country and $61.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold $0.50 higher at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants, the dealers said.
